name: Rattail

image.caption: Child in the 1980's with a rattail

lead: A rattail is a hairstyle in which the hair is short except for a single long, thin strand left to hang at the back of the neck. Wearers use it as a distinctive, retro or alternative style.
It has roots going back to the Manchu queue, was popular in the 1980s, faded by the mid-1990s and returned around 2015, according to Wikipedia.

paras: The tail is grown out from the nape and can hang loose or be braided, dyed, permed or curled. It is often paired with shaved or short sides.
Few risks; very thin hair strands may tangle or break, and the style may draw varied reactions.

chain: Keep a long tail at the nape
angle.text: The tail is a styling choice that changes the silhouette of a short cut. It is paired with shaved sides or dyed in punk-style versions.

lead: A rattail is a hairstyle with a long, tail-like section of hair at the back of the head, longer than the rest of the hair. It can hang loose or be braided, dreaded, permed, straightened or curled.[1]
A rattail is a narrower variant of the mullet idea: the mullet is short at front and sides and long behind, while a rattail leaves just a single long strand.[2]

Wikipedia traces it to the 17th-century Manchu queue, notes a mid-to-late-1980s peak, a mid-1990s decline and a return around 2015, described as a "rattail renaissance" in a 2023 Wall Street Journal piece.[1]

paras: Variations include braided, dreaded, permed or multiple tails, the Polynesian "horsetail", and punk versions with dyed tails.[1]

Wikipedia lists musicians who wore it, including Jordan Knight, Neil Peart and Curt Smith, and cites its popularity in Broome in Western Australia and in New Zealand among boys.[1] Greg Prato suggested Peart may have been among the first rock musicians to wear one.[2]
